title: WorkManager
objectives: Know when WorkManager is and isn't the right tool

sections.markdown: WorkManager is the recommended API for persistent, deferrable background work that must run even across app restarts and device reboots — it chooses the best underlying scheduler for the OS version.

Use WorkManager for **guaranteed, deferrable** work (upload logs, sync, backups). Do NOT use it for immediate, exact-time, or in-process tasks — use coroutines for those, AlarmManager for exact alarms, and foreground services for ongoing user-visible work.
Expecting WorkManager to run at an exact instant. It's deferrable — the system batches work for battery efficiency. For exact timing use AlarmManager (sparingly).

flashcards.back: Guaranteed, deferrable background work that must survive app restarts/reboots (sync, upload, backup).
Network connectivity, charging, device idle, sufficient battery/storage.
WorkManager = deferrable guaranteed work; AlarmManager = exact-time alarms (use sparingly).

quiz.explain: It guarantees deferrable work runs, even after reboot.
Constraints, backoff retries and work chaining are core features.

quiz.q: For an immediate one-off task while the app is open, prefer…
quiz.explain: Coroutines handle immediate in-process async work; WorkManager is for deferrable/guaranteed work.

challenges.text: Create a Worker that logs and run it once with enqueue().
Add a network constraint and exponential backoff to an upload worker.
Chain compress → upload → notify workers and pass data between them.
Implement periodic sync with unique work and observe state via WorkInfo LiveData.
